title: Level Crossings & Tramways
whatItIs: At level crossings trains always have priority. Trams run on fixed rails, so they can't steer round you.

keyFacts.text: You MUST obey the flashing red lights at a level crossing and stop.
If the lights keep flashing after a train has passed, you MUST wait: another train is coming.

keyFacts: Never stop on a level crossing. In queues, keep the crossing clear.
Broken down on a crossing? Get everyone out and clear first, then phone the signal operator.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT enter a road, lane or route reserved for trams.

keyFacts: Trams can be quiet and can't steer round you: never stop on the tracks.

visual.caption: At a crossing with lights and barriers

items.title: Amber light and alarm
items.text: Stop, unless you have already crossed the stop line.

items.title: Flashing red lights
items.text: You MUST stop and wait behind the white line.

items.title: Barriers come down
items.text: Never zigzag round them or move onto the crossing.

items.title: Train passes
items.text: Lights still flashing? Another train is coming: keep waiting.

items.title: Lights off, barriers up
items.text: Cross when the way is clear, without stopping on it.

a.label: Steady amber
points: Stop unless you've crossed the line

onTheTest.question: At a level crossing, the red lights keep flashing after a train has passed. What should you do?
options: Wait, because another train is coming
onTheTest.why: If the lights keep flashing after a train passes, another train is coming. Wait until the lights go off and the barriers rise.

traps: Broken down on the crossing: people out first, then phone.
A tram can't swerve: keep off tram tracks when you stop.
